summary: Small-system flow response leads the daily selection: a hydrodynamics-versus-kinetic-theory comparison establishes a robust Ne+Ne/O+O elliptic-flow ratio, while O+O strangeness ordering, neon fragmentation, and hyperon spin correlations supply targeted phenomenology. The physics-ML highlights are data-efficient stationary-field surrogates, semiparametric PDF inference, and memory-aware reduced dynamics.
professional_summary: O+O and Ne+Ne flow response, transverse-density ordering, spectator fragmentation, chiral-imbalance spin correlations, neural surrogate simulation, semiparametric PDF inference, and Mori-Zwanzig closure define the selected literature.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2611.05239 is the strongest result: its direct hydrodynamics-versus-kinetic-theory comparison shows that the Ne+Ne/O+O elliptic-flow ratio is robust to the evolution model, while triangular flow remains sensitive to nonequilibrium dynamics.

papers.title: Elliptic and triangular flow responses in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions from hydrodynamics and kinetic theory
papers.short_authors: Victor E. Ambrus, Giuliano Giacalone, Clemens Werthmann, Fabian Zhou
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic and relaxation-time kinetic-theory calculations are compared across opacities for O+O and Ne+Ne collisions. Ne-to-O elliptic-flow ratios remain stable across the dynamical descriptions, whereas triangular-flow ratios retain appreciable nonequilibrium sensitivity.
papers.summary: A controlled hydrodynamics-versus-kinetic-theory comparison shows that the Ne+Ne/O+O v2 ratio is a robust nuclear-geometry observable, while the corresponding v3 ratio is a sharper probe of incomplete hydrodynamization.
papers.critical_assessment: The strongest paper in the batch. It tests the key inference across dynamical frameworks and a broad opacity range using ab-initio-informed nuclear inputs. The remaining caveat is that conformal RTA is still a simplified kinetic theory, so robustness against more realistic transport and pre-equilibrium dynamics remains to be shown.

papers.title: Probing the Spatial Coherence of Chiral-Imbalance Fluctuations with Hyperon Spin Correlations
papers.short_authors: Guangyu Zheng, Zilin Yuan, Mei Huang, Guannan Xie
papers.abstract: AMPT calculations with imposed axial-chemical-potential domains propose differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a probe of chiral-imbalance magnitude and spatial coherence. A short-to-long-range ratio varies strongly with the imposed domain scale and only weakly with the explored mu5 magnitude.
papers.summary: The proposed common-mode hyperon-pair correlation separates fluctuation strength from coherence scale and supplies an experimentally defined short-to-long-range ratio.
papers.critical_assessment: A clever observable-level proposal with explicit channel combinations and a thermal-vorticity/shear baseline. However, the signal is generated by an imposed mu5 field inside one transport framework, the explored mu5 values are model choices, and common-mode hadronization backgrounds are not cancelled; experimental feasibility and background closure are not yet established.

papers.title: Multiplicity and transverse density as ordering variables of the Lambda/K0S ratio in oxygen-oxygen collisions at the LHC
papers.abstract: Published CMS O+O, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb data are reweighted to test whether equal multiplicity organizes the Lambda/K0S spectral shape. Equal transverse density improves cross-system agreement, with the result depending on the modeled transverse size of high-multiplicity p-Pb events.
papers.summary: The data reject multiplicity as a sufficient cross-system ordering variable for the Lambda/K0S shape and favor transverse density, while predicting similar minimum-bias O+O and Ne+Ne ratios.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong for a compact phenomenology study: it uses published data, propagates covariance alternatives, compares EPOS4 and Angantyr, and makes a near-term Ne+Ne prediction. The decisive p-Pb matching requires subnucleonic Glauber structure, so the hydrodynamic interpretation remains conditional on modeled overlap area.

papers.title: Modeling fragmentation of 20Ne nuclei at the LHC
papers.short_authors: Aleksandr Svetlichnyi, Savva Savenkov, Igor Pshenichnov
papers.abstract: An abrasion-ablation Monte Carlo with pre-equilibrium spectator clustering, fragment decay, and Coulomb repulsion is validated against legacy neon-fragmentation data and extrapolated to 20Ne+20Ne at 5.36 TeV. Forward fragment yields and momentum distributions are evaluated for beam transport and ZDC studies.
papers.summary: The paper provides experimentally useful forward-fragment inputs and quantifies sensitivity to Woods-Saxon, spherical, and five-alpha neon configurations.
papers.critical_assessment: Useful and unusually concrete for LHC operations and forward-detector simulation, with validation against existing fragmentation data. The extrapolation to collider energy is model-dependent, and the nuclear-structure discrimination is entangled with the MST clustering prescription; this is a simulation input, not yet a demonstrated structure measurement.

papers.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation
papers.abstract: Macrocanonical generator networks learn stationary physical processes by matching multiscale feature statistics in expectation. Tests on MHD turbulence and cosmological density fields show realistic held-out statistics from very small training sets and large sampling speedups after amortized training.
papers.summary: A symmetry-aware generator recovers sample-to-sample fluctuations from as little as one stationary field, beats standard generative baselines in the low-data regime, and improves downstream cosmological inference.
papers.critical_assessment: The strongest physics-ML paper today: accepted at NeurIPS, theoretically motivated, tested against held-out simulations and WGAN, flow-matching, and diffusion baselines, with an SBI demonstration. Transfer to heavy-ion event fields is credible only where approximate stationarity and chosen statistics are defensible; nonstationary geometries, boundaries, centrality conditioning, and collapse guarantees remain open.

papers.title: Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions
papers.short_authors: Huanbiao Zhu, Jaco ter Hoeve, Mikael Kuusela, Maria Ubiali, Larry Wasserman
papers.abstract: A semiparametric one-step estimator uses the efficient influence function to debias physics-parameter estimates for uncertainty in an infinite-dimensional PDF nuisance without rerunning a full joint fit. Toy DIS studies recover nominal frequentist coverage.
papers.summary: The method rigorously corrects decoupled physics-parameter estimates for PDF interplay and restores coverage without a computationally costly simultaneous fit.
papers.critical_assessment: Not a neural-network paper, but arguably more consequential for precision HEP than most ML applications in this batch. The statistical construction and coverage tests are strong; evidence is still limited to two preparatory toy scenarios, so scaling to realistic correlated global PDF fits and theory systematics is the real test.

papers.title: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems
papers.short_authors: Emily Williams, Saad Qadeer, Amanda Howard, Panos Stinis
papers.abstract: Physics-informed learned bases are combined with Mori-Zwanzig memory kernels and a generative subgrid closure. On viscous Burgers dynamics, both closures reduce filtered-state error relative to Markovian evolution.
papers.summary: Memory-aware closures lower average relative error from 6.6% to 2.9% for the FDT model and 2.4% for the generative closure on the demonstrated Burgers problem.
papers.critical_assessment: The formal connection between learned bases, memory, and stochastic closure is valuable and relevant to coarse-grained transport. Validation is narrow: one one-dimensional viscous Burgers setup, one principal initial-condition family, increasing long-time error, and costly fine stepping for the explicit memory integral. Heavy-ion transfer is plausible but unproven.

cautions.title: Deep Learning for Longitudinal Asymmetry in Heavy-Ion Collisions at RHIC Energies
cautions.short_authors: Anup Kumar Sikdar, Sanchari Thakur, Pingal Dasgupta, Rupa Chatterjee
cautions.abstract: A fully connected network emulates AMPT event-level longitudinal asymmetry and rapidity-shift quantities across Au+Au and Cu+Cu systems and several RHIC energies, including centrality intervals withheld from training.
cautions.summary: The network reproduces AMPT targets and interpolates across held-out centrality intervals, with SHAP used to inspect feature dependence.
cautions.critical_assessment: Potentially useful as an emulator, but the paper does not compare against linear, polynomial, tree-based, or analytic baselines even though several target relations are strongly constrained by kinematics. Held-out centrality intervals are interpolation within the same generator, not transfer to another model or data, and the downstream flow effect is small after event averaging. The scientific claim should remain modest.
